title: India's Women Beat Bangladesh 3-0 in Goa. They Have Not Conceded a Goal in the SAFF Championship.
excerpt: Fourteen goals scored, zero conceded. The Blue Tigresses topped Group B and will face Bhutan in the semi-finals after dismantling the defending champions in Margao.
body:
India's women beat Bangladesh 3-0 at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Margao on Sunday evening to top Group B of the SAFF Women's Championship 2026 with a perfect record. Two wins from two matches, fourteen goals scored, none conceded.

Pyari Xaxa opened the scoring in the 36th minute. Lynda Kom converted from the penalty spot in the 78th. Malavika Prasad headed home in the 91st to seal a result that was more comfortable than the scoreline suggests.

## Six Changes, One Clear Intent

Head coach Crispin Chettri made six changes to the side that had thrashed Maldives 11-0 in the tournament opener. Panthoi Chanu replaced Shreya in goal. Three new defenders came in. Sanfida returned to midfield. Soumya Guguloth started on the wing. And in a notable tactical experiment, Aveka Singh was deployed as a lone striker, with Xaxa moved out wide.

The changes disrupted India's rhythm early. The game was end-to-end in the opening exchanges, with poor defensive communication gifting Bangladesh several half-chances. But once India settled, they dominated possession and territory, creating chance after chance.

The problem was finishing. India missed multiple clear opportunities before Xaxa's strike shortly before half-time. The Blue Tigresses went into the break with a slender 1-0 lead that flattered their opponents.

## Bangladesh Push Back, India Close the Door

Bangladesh, the defending SAFF Women's champions, came out with attacking intent in the second half. They created promising opportunities of their own but lacked the clinical edge to convert. The pattern mirrored their 4-2 win over Maldives earlier in the group stage — competitive, aggressive, but vulnerable when stretched.

India continued to create and continued to waste chances. It took a penalty in the 78th minute, won and dispatched by Kom, to give the Blue Tigresses breathing room. Prasad's stoppage-time header removed any remaining doubt.

## What Comes Next

India top Group B with six points and a goal difference of plus-14. Bangladesh finish second with three points and progress to the knockout stage as well. Both teams had already qualified before kick-off — this match determined seedings, not survival.

India will face Bhutan in the semi-finals. Bangladesh will meet Nepal. The knockout rounds continue through to the final on June 6, all in Goa.

For the Indian diaspora watching on FanCode, the result carries weight beyond the SAFF tournament. The Women's T20 Cricket World Cup begins in England next month. The FIFA Women's World Cup qualification cycle is in motion. Indian women's sport is no longer a sideshow that appears once every four years at the Olympics. These are real campaigns, with real stakes, unfolding in real time.

The attendance at Margao was 553. Small by IPL final standards. But every tournament starts somewhere, and India's women are building something worth watching.

The tournament runs from May 25 to June 6 at the Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Margao, Goa. All matches are streamed live on FanCode in India.
